title: The war shifts: Castile has raised some 5,000 men and drives the Moroccans back from raiding its heartlands, while in Aragon and on the islands Tunisian and other Moorish raiders sack the countryside freely
source: Trent's account (by July 1350; the exact day isn't given)

title: As the pestilence fades, the reckoning: the old lands of Granada have lost 42% of their people since August 1346, among the worst in the world; Iberia as a whole a third, Castile 35%, Aragon 33%, Portugal 30%; Morocco only 19% and Tunis 7%; the world some 46 million souls
source: saves of 1346-08-01 and 1350-09-02 (same lands compared); Trent's screenshot of the Black Death panel

title: The realm steadies as the plague passes: stability back to 12.6, and sovereignty climbing to 58.8

The cities bore the worst of it. Granada was the most urban realm in Iberia, with 41% of its people in cities against Castile's 5%, and its cities lost 45% of their people despite the hospitals. Burghers fell by 60% and the clergy and scholars by 53%, while the soldiers in camp lost only 15%. Castile's few cities lost only 22%
source: saves of 1346-08-01 and 1350-09-02, populations by settlement rank and pop type over the same lands

title: Aragon makes peace with the Moorish powers: Morocco takes the Balearic Islands and Tunis subjugates Aragon's Sardinian vassal, the County of Cagliari. All eyes turn to the Strait, where Castile has pushed south to Cádiz
